sections.1.heading: Invoicing software for contractors: who it suits
sections.1.body:
The word contractor covers two very different jobs, and it's worth being clear which one Paidlyo serves. **Invoicing software for contractors** in construction and the trades needs materials, progress billing, retentions and job site estimates. Paidlyo has none of that, so if you're an electrical, painting or general contractor, a construction-focused tool will suit you far better.

Paidlyo is for **independent contractors who sell hours under a contract**: developers, engineers, designers, consultants, analysts, writers and other professionals who work for a client for weeks or months at an agreed hourly rate. It's also for small agencies that place contractors with clients and bill their hours.

For that kind of work, the invoice is simple in shape but easy to get wrong in detail. It has to match the contract, use the right rates, cover the right period and reach the right person. Paidlyo builds it from the hours you tracked: each contract is a project, each type of work is a task with its own rate, and the invoice draft is built from every unbilled hour in one click.

In the example above, one month under one contract becomes two clear lines, with on-call hours billed at the premium the contract allows.

sections.2.heading: Matching the client's paperwork
sections.2.body:
Contract clients, especially larger companies and recruitment agencies, often check invoices against their own records before paying. A few habits get invoices approved the first time:

1. **One project per contract or statement of work.** Hours for different contracts never mix, and each invoice covers one agreement.
2. **Task names that match the contract.** If the contract says "Development" and "On-call support", use exactly those.
3. **The contract or purchase order reference** in the email you send with the invoice link, plus any reference the client's accounts team asked for.
4. **The right period.** Invoice the hours for the agreed period, such as a calendar month, and nothing else.
5. **The right person.** Send the link to whoever approves invoices, as well as your day-to-day contact.

In Paidlyo, you review the draft before sharing it. You can rename lines, add tax and choose whether lines are grouped by project, task or person. The client opens the invoice through a private link without an account, and can save a PDF for their records.
sections.3.heading: Weekly or monthly invoices?
sections.3.body:
How often you invoice decides how much unpaid work you carry. Using the example contract, with payment terms of 14 days:

| Invoice cadence | Typical invoice | Longest stretch of work not yet paid |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly | About $14,700 | About 6 weeks |
| Every two weeks | About $7,400 | About 4 weeks |
| Weekly | About $3,700 | About 3 weeks |

Monthly invoicing is simpler for both sides, and many clients prefer it. Weekly or fortnightly invoicing reduces your risk if a client pays late or a contract ends suddenly.

Because Paidlyo builds invoices from unbilled hours, any cadence works. At the end of each period, create the invoice for that client. Hours already invoiced aren't picked up again, so each invoice covers exactly the work since the last one.

Whatever you choose, agree it in the contract, then stick to it. Predictable invoices make it easier for the client's accounts team to pay you on time, because they know what's coming and when.
sections.4.heading: Late payments and partial payments
sections.4.body:
Contractors are often paid through several layers: a client's accounts team, sometimes a recruitment agency, sometimes a payroll provider. Payments can arrive late, split, or short.

Record every payment in Paidlyo as it arrives, in full or in part. A partly paid invoice stays open with the correct balance. The outstanding invoices report then lists everything unpaid by age, so you can see at a glance which invoices need chasing.

A simple chasing routine:

- **On the due date:** check the report and confirm nothing is missing.
- **A few days late:** a short, polite reminder with the invoice link.
- **Two weeks late:** contact the person who approves invoices, not only your project contact.
- **A month late:** raise it formally, using the payment terms in your contract.

Clients can't pay by card through Paidlyo. They pay you directly, by bank transfer or however your contract says, and you record it.
sections.5.heading: Tax, currency and what Paidlyo doesn't do
sections.5.body:
Contractors often work across borders. Each client in Paidlyo has their own currency, so a client abroad can be invoiced in the currency in your contract. You can add a tax percentage to an invoice, but whether tax applies, and at what rate, depends on your registration and where the client is. Ask your accountant before the first invoice to a new country.

It's also worth knowing the limits:

- **No expenses.** Travel and equipment costs need to be invoiced from another tool.
- **No recurring or fixed-amount invoices.** Every invoice is built from tracked hours.
- **No accounting integration.** You can export hours and outstanding invoices to CSV.
- **No card payments or mobile app.** Clients pay you directly, and you work from a browser.

For the tracking side, such as hour caps and different rates under one contract, see [time tracking for contractors](/time-tracking/for/contractors). If you bill larger companies as a consultant, [invoicing for consultants](/invoicing/for/consultants) covers procurement and approval in more depth. Paidlyo costs $9 per person a month.

faq.1.question: Is Paidlyo suitable for construction contractors?
faq.1.answer: No. Paidlyo invoices hours only, with no materials, progress billing or retentions. It suits contractors who bill hourly under a contract.
faq.2.question: Can I invoice weekly?
faq.2.answer: Yes. Invoices are built from unbilled hours, so you can create one at the end of any period, weekly or monthly.
faq.3.question: Can I bill on-call hours at a higher rate?
faq.3.answer: Yes. Create a task for on-call work with its own hourly rate, and invoice lines use it automatically.
faq.4.question: Can I invoice clients in another currency?
faq.4.answer: Yes. Each client has their own currency, and every invoice to that client uses it.
